question: Shape follows from how a molecule is built, and what it can do follows from its shape: that chain of reasoning is the _____ molecular biology runs on.
questions: Nearly half of human protein-coding genes carry long segments with no stable fold, which is the standing exception to the _____ rather than a failure of folding.
One protein taking several different amyloid folds, each tied to a different disease, shows that one sequence does not always fix one shape, which the _____ quietly assumes.
abstract:
The structure-function relationship is the organising assumption of molecular biology, so settled that the papers questioning it are titled as going beyond a paradigm: what a molecule does follows from its shape, and its shape follows from how it is built. A protein is the standard demonstration, since its conformation is determined by its amino acid sequence, with hydrophobic side chains sorting into the interior and hydrophilic ones onto the surface. The chain has preferred shapes at all only because the peptide bond is planar and permits no rotation, while the other backbone bonds do, which sharply restricts what conformations are available. The bonds that then hold a fold are individually thirty to three hundred times weaker than a covalent bond, so a structure is stable without being rigid. Where the reasoning bites hardest is at a single position: replacing a glutamate with a valine at the sixth place in the beta-globin chain gives haemoglobin S.

The relationship is not universal, and nearly half of human protein-coding genes contain long disordered segments that never settle into a stable three-dimensional fold. Those regions are not failures of folding but work as shifting ensembles, carrying out signalling, transcriptional regulation, chromatin organisation and the assembly of organelles without membranes. The other half of the assumption fails too, since a single protein can take up several different amyloid folds, and the ones adopted by prion protein, tau, alpha-synuclein and TDP-43 differ between neurodegenerative diseases. So one sequence does not always specify one shape, and the flexibility comes from the packing interactions themselves rather than from any change in the chain. What survives is a rule of thumb of enormous power rather than a law, and knowing where it does not hold is part of knowing how to use it.
